title: When the Colony Sings
premise: Rafael Brightwater, the last xenolinguist on the failing colony of Meridian's Rest, has spent years recording the dying songs of a native species no one on Earth believes exists. When the deep-space vessel Halcyon returns with its crew mysteriously aged backward, they bring official records declaring Meridian's Rest never suffered its founding massacre—and Rafael, who survived it as a child, is the only living witness. As Earth's final transmission loop counts down to permanent silence, she must decode the native songs she's archived into proof of what happened, discovering that the aliens' 'songs' are actually testimony. The novel ends with Rafael broadcasting the translated massacre record in both human and native languages as the loop closes, choosing belonging with the colony's ghosts over rescue by people who erased her.
about_author: S. M. Vane is the pen name of a former field linguist who spent six years documenting endangered oral traditions before turning to fiction. They write from a coastal town where fog rolls in most mornings, insisting it helps them hear dialogue better.

chapters.title: The Last Fluent Speaker
chapters.summary: Rafael records the final song of an elderly native creature called a Vessel, whose language she alone partially understands. Her POV establishes her isolation, her fading ability to dream in English, and the colony's decay. Emotional beat: quiet grief disguised as professional routine.

chapters.title: Loop Forty-One
chapters.summary: Rafael monitors Earth's transmission loop—automated messages repeating on a 400-day cycle—and realizes the interval is shortening. Colony administrator Dessa Okonkwo dismisses her concerns. POV shifts briefly to Dessa, revealing she knows more than she admits. Beat: creeping dread beneath bureaucratic calm.

chapters.title: What the Children Buried
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: nine-year-old Rafael hides in a root cellar during the Founding Massacre, hearing screams in two languages. Present-day Rafael returns to the sealed cellar and finds a child's carved tally marks. Beat: trauma surfacing through physical space.

chapters.title: A Ship Younger Than Its Voyage
chapters.summary: The Halcyon descends, carrying crew members who left as adults but returned as children—the same faces, decades younger. Rafael recognizes Commander Ilsa Reyes, now twelve years old. Beat: uncanny wonder curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: Official History
chapters.summary: The child-crew presents Earth's records: Meridian's Rest was founded peacefully; no massacre occurred; the Vessels were never sentient. Rafael's own colonial file lists her as deceased. Beat: gaslighting at civilizational scale.

chapters.title: Dessa's Bargain
chapters.summary: Dessa privately tells Rafael the child-crew carries authority to evacuate everyone before the loop ends—but only if the colonists sign the revised history. Dessa urges signing. Rafael refuses. Beat: loyalty tested against survival.

chapters.title: Songs Are Testimony
chapters.summary: Working through her archive at night, Rafael realizes the Vessel songs aren't art—they're structured witness accounts, each one naming human perpetrators. The old Vessel's final song names the massacre's architect: Ilsa Reyes, adult version. Beat: revelation that reframes everything.

chapters.title: Twelve Years Old, Twice
chapters.summary: Rafael confronts child-Ilsa, who remembers nothing but dreams of fire. Meanwhile the ship's doctor, also de-aged, shows signs of recovered memories breaking through. Beat: pity warring with fury.

chapters.title: The Erasure Engine
chapters.summary: Rafael infiltrates the Halcyon and finds the device that reversed the crew's ages—it edits neural records, and its logs show it was used on the colony's archives too. Beat: horror of technology weaponized against memory itself.

chapters.title: Colonists Who Signed
chapters.summary: Half the colony signs the false history for evacuation slots. Rafael's few allies begin receiving threats. Her closest friend, machinist Teodor, signs and won't meet her eyes. Beat: betrayal and the seduction of forgetting.

chapters.title: Dreaming in Vessel
chapters.summary: Rafael stops dreaming in any human language entirely; instead she dreams the Vessel songs whole, understanding them completely for the first time. She wakes knowing where massacre survivors hid their own counter-records. Beat: transformation—her estrangement becomes fluency.

chapters.title: The Bone Archive
chapters.summary: Guided by her dreams, Rafael excavates a Vessel ossuary containing resonant bone-lattices that store recorded memory. They hold the massacre in perfect detail—including the fact that the de-aging tech was first tested there. Beat: awe and desecration intertwined.

chapters.title: Quarantine
chapters.summary: Child-Ilsa, recovering memories, tries to testify and is confined by the ship's remaining adult-ranking officers—who turn out to be corporate custodians riding inside the de-aged bodies' legal authority. Beat: the machinery of power exposed.

chapters.title: Teodor's Confession
chapters.summary: Teodor admits he signed because his daughter is aboard the evacuation list, then secretly gives Rafael the maintenance codes to the colony's broadcast array. Beat: forgiveness without absolution.

chapters.title: The Loop Shortens
chapters.summary: Earth's transmission loop accelerates wildly—the custodians are forcing the final cycle early to make the false history permanent before anyone can object. Hours remain, not days. Beat: ticking clock engaged.

chapters.title: Every Record Says Otherwise
chapters.summary: Rafael assembles her case: bone-lattices, song translations, the erasure engine's logs. But the custodians legally control all verification channels. Proof exists; no forum will hear it. Beat: despair at the edge of climax.

chapters.title: Breaking Ilsa Open
chapters.summary: Rafael frees child-Ilsa and plays her the Vessel song bearing her adult name. Ilsa's memories return in a flood—she ordered the massacre under orders she can now name. Beat: devastating witness reclaimed.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax: Rafael, Ilsa, and Teodor seize the broadcast array and transmit the massacre record in English and Vessel simultaneously into the closing loop, hijacking Earth's final message channel. Custodians storm the array. Beat: sacrifice against the deadline.

chapters.title: What Earth Hears Last
chapters.summary: The loop closes carrying the truth. The custodians are arrested by their own crew once Ilsa's restored authority surfaces. But the victory costs the ossuary, destroyed in the assault. Beat: triumph shadowed by loss.

chapters.title: Evacuation Refused
chapters.summary: The Halcyon offers rescue. Rafael declines, and most colonists stay with her—the colony belongs to those who remember it. Dessa, finally honest, chooses to remain and rebuild the archive. Beat: chosen belonging over offered escape.

chapters.title: First New Song
chapters.summary: Months later, the surviving Vessels—more remained than believed—begin teaching Rafael their language properly. She records not a death but a beginning: a song composed jointly, in both tongues. Beat: inheritance passed forward.

chapters.title: When the Colony Sings
chapters.summary: Years on, a new transmission arrives from Earth—not a loop but a voice, responding to what they sent. Rafael, dreaming now only in Vessel, answers in both languages. Final beat: the forgotten colony becomes the ones who remembered for everyone.
